Legendary plays Legend Entertainment's adventure games, from 1990 to 1995, from copies you have: *Spellcasting 101*, *Timequest*, *Spellcasting 201*, *Gateway*, *Spellcasting 301*, *Eric the Unready*, *Gateway II: Homeworld*, *Companions of Xanth* and *Mission Critical*. No game is included.

## Playing

Download the file for your computer, unpack it, and run `legendary` in the folder (`legendary.exe` on Windows) with your copy of a game's folder: `legendary "<the game's folder>"`. A folder given once is remembered, and the game is then started by its short name, as `legendary sc101`; with no game named, a menu lists the ones it knows. `legendary --help` lists the rest, and the [README](https://github.com/jeffnyman/legendary#readme) says what each game needs, such as the files from its CD.

| Download | For |
|---|---|
| `win-x64` (zip) | Windows, 64-bit |
| `linux-x64` (tar.gz) | Linux, 64-bit |
| `osx-arm64` (tar.gz) | macOS on Apple silicon |
| `osx-x64` (tar.gz) | macOS on Intel |

The programs aren't signed. Windows may ask before running one from the internet (More info, then Run anyway). macOS keeps it from opening until it's allowed: in the unpacked folder, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in a terminal, or allow it in System Settings, Privacy & Security.

Saves and settings go in a `Legendary` folder in your user's application data; the games' own files are never changed.
